subject: DPIA evidence - Article 28/30 ledger extract & KMS wrap clarification
body:
From: Oliver Barnes <oliver.barnes@meditech.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: security@meditech.com
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 09:12:00 +0000
Subject: DPIA evidence request - ledger extract & KMS details

Hi Irene,

Thanks for taking this. As part of our final DPIA review for the MediTech integration (scope: clinical notes extraction, anonymised metrics), our security and legal teams need a short package of evidence to close Art. 28 / Art. 30 questions. In particular:

- A short ledger extract showing processing activities for the Meditech tenant (fields: dataset id, processing purpose, subprocessors touched, last access time).
- KMS wrapping details and a diagram showing where keys are held, wrap/un-wrap operations, and HSM/KMS provider names.
- Confirmation of any cross-border subprocessors involved in processing personal data and the transfer mechanism (SCCs, onshore routing, other).

We are on a tight timeline for a March 18 audit gate. Can you provide the ledger extract and KMS diagram by end-of-week? If some items require an ops walk-through, we can schedule a short call. Also cc'ing our security mailbox to keep them in loop.

Thanks,
Oliver Barnes
Head of Security, MediTech

Hi Oliver — thanks for the clear list.

We can provide:
- A CSV extract of the Art.30 ledger filtered to the MediTech tenant (sampled rows to protect other customers) — will include dataset id, processing purpose, subprocessors, processing locations, and last-modified timestamps.
- A one-page KMS wrap diagram that shows where keys are generated, wrapped, and stored, and the KMS provider names we use (cloud KMS + optional customer-managed HSM).
- A short narrative describing transfer mechanisms for each subprocessor and whether SCCs or onshore routing are used.

Questions from our side:
1) Do you need a full ledger export or a representative sample for audit consumption? (you mentioned "extract" but want to confirm)
2) Is there a preferred format for the KMS diagram (PNG/PDF) and any level of detail the auditor needs?

Internal folks tagged: Marissa (privacy ops) — can you prepare the ledger extract and proposed sampling approach? Karthik — can you confirm KMS wrap diagram and the canonical list of subprocessors for MediTech? Naomi — FYI from legal for any redline on disclosures.

Irene Choi

From: karthik.iyer@redwood.com
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, irene.choi@redwood.com
Cc: Oliver Barnes <oliver.barnes@meditech.com>
Date: Fri, 5 Mar 2027 15:05:54 +0000
Subject: Re: DPIA evidence request - ledger extract & KMS details

Hi all — attaching the KMS wrap diagram (kms-wrap-diagram.png) and a short write-up (dpia-impact-summary.pdf) that explains the key wrapping flow we use and where the customer tenant encryption keys live. Summary:

- Keys: Tenant data keys are wrapped with a tenant envelope key; the envelope key is stored in our primary cloud KMS. Customers on Dedicated can opt to bring their own keys (BYOK) and we support HSM providers for that flow.
- HSM/KMS providers: Primary: Redwood KMS (managed KMS backed by AWS KMS in eu-west-1), Backup: customer BYOK via vendor HSM (optional).
- Subprocessors: list included in the write-up (short): infra-monitoring vendor (InfraLook), analytics provider (VectraMetrics) — both process only pseudonymised telemetry; InfraLook has an EU-only routing option enabled for MediTech.
- Cross-border transfers: For InfraLook and analytics vendor we either: (a) route EU tenant workload to EU-only pools, or (b) fall back to SCCs where routing is not feasible. No U.S. access to raw PD for MediTech.
- Art.30 register path: ledger extract will include ID pointers to our Art.30 register export. We can provide a PDF excerpt for the auditor but cannot export the full register with other customers' entries — we will provide scoped excerpts showing MediTech rows.

I created RED-4567 to track the ledger extraction work and gave Marissa access.

If you need signed confirmation of the transfer mechanism (attestation), let me know and we can route that through Legal / Contracts for a DPA addendum.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Infrastructure Security
Redwood Inference

Irene/Marissa/Karthik — thanks for the fast turnaround and the materials so far. The security team reviewed the snippet and the KMS write-up: helpful. A couple of remaining asks before we close our gate:

1) Formal attestation on routing: can Redwood provide a signed attestation that MediTech tenant processing is EU-only (no U.S. access to raw PD) unless explicit written exception is granted?
2) DocuSign for a short DPA addendum: procurement will need a signature path that references the KMS and transfer controls. Can someone from Contracts/Legal produce a one-page attestation and a DPA addendum template?

If you can put both items in DocuSign (procurement@meditech.com is on copy) we can close the DPIA review this week. Happy to take a short call if useful.

Best,
Oliver
Head of Security, MediTech
